title: Early Atlas Progression and Waystone Sustain
summary: How to start the Path of Exile 2 endgame Atlas without running out of maps: Doryani's first map, Hilda's boss passive, waystone sustain nodes, towers with precursor tablets, and the 3-to-1 reforge.
description: A practical early-Atlas routing guide for Path of Exile 2: how to keep your map pool growing instead of drying up.
prerequisites: Campaign completed on at least one character
Access to the Ziggurat Encampment and the Atlas map screen
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team

items.title: What keeps maps going?
body: Waystone sustain comes from three places: running maps drops more waystones, the Atlas passive tree has explicit sustain nodes (for example Constant Crossroads, Fortunate Path, and High Road), and you can reforge three lower-tier waystones into one higher-tier waystone at the reforging bench.

items.title: First steps after the campaign
body: Enter Doryani's first map from the Ziggurat, clear it, then talk to Hilda to unlock a powerful boss-passive node on your Atlas tree. That node powers up every subsequent boss you kill.

items.title: Why are towers important?
body: Towers let you socket precursor tablets that add modifiers to every map in their radius. A single tablet can upgrade an entire region's waystone drops and rewards.

sections.title: Progression: maps, towers, tablets
sections.intro: The first hours of Atlas are a loop of three activities. Switch tabs to see what each is for.

tabs.label: Run maps
paragraphs: Your basic fuel. Each map you complete can drop waystones for that tier or higher.
bullets: Start with the tier of waystone you have; do not skip tiers or you will starve.
Use Hilda's boss passive node - it strengthens every boss, improving map-boss loot.
If a map feels too hard, drop down a tier rather than burning your only high-tier stone.

tabs.label: Capture towers
paragraphs: Towers are special map nodes that, once cleared, let you slot precursor tablets.
bullets: Each tower has 3 precursor tablet slots.
A tablet modifies every map inside the tower's radius, including waystone drop rate and reward type.
Prioritise towers whose radius covers maps you are actively running.

tabs.label: Apply tablets
paragraphs: Precursor tablets are the lever that turns a normal region into a sustain engine.
bullets: Match tablet modifiers to your goal: waystone sustain, currency, or specific league mechanics.
Stack overlapping tower radii for stronger combined effects.
Reforge excess low-tier waystones (3-to-1) instead of vendoring them.

sections.title: Your first Atlas objectives
sections.intro: Hit these in order during your first session in the Atlas.

cards.title: Doryani's first map
body: The guaranteed first map after the campaign. Clear it to open the Atlas and trigger Hilda's passive unlock.

cards.title: Talk to Hilda
body: After your first map boss, Hilda grants a powerful boss-passive node. Allocate it before farming further.

cards.title: Clear a nearby tower
body: Capture the closest tower and socket precursor tablets covering the maps you plan to run.

cards.title: Run the Precursor Fortress
body: A special map that advances your Atlas. Prioritise it when it appears in your radius.

sections.title: Why are my maps running out?
sections.intro: Pick the symptom you are seeing. The tool points to the missing lever.

rules.title: You are skipping tiers or not running in sequence
steps: Run maps at the tier you actually have waystones for; do not leap tiers.
Each completed map drops waystones of equal or higher tier - consistent running refills the pool.
Use the 3-to-1 reforge to rebuild a higher tier from leftovers.

rules.title: You burned your only high-tier stones
steps: Drop back down a tier and rebuild using sustain nodes and reforges.
Allocate Constant Crossroads / Fortunate Path / High Road on the Atlas tree.
Stop using high-tier stones in maps you cannot clear comfortably.

rules.title: Improve gear before pushing tier
steps: Cap resistances and fix life/defenses first; a dead character drops no maps.
Use Hilda's boss passive and tower tablets to make maps easier, not harder.

rules.title: Allocate Hilda's boss passive and use towers
steps: Talk to Hilda after your first map boss to unlock the boss passive node.
Socket precursor tablets in towers over your farming region to boost boss rewards.

defaultResult.title: General sustain recovery
steps: Run maps in tier order, allocate sustain Atlas nodes, and capture towers with tablets.
Reforge three low-tier waystones into one higher tier rather than vendoring them.
If stuck, watch the referenced endgame progression guide for a full visual route.

entries.description: A full early-Atlas routing guide covering waystone sustain, the Precursor Fortress, Hilda's passive trick, tower and tablet strategy, and the biggest mistakes players make.
entries.takeaway: Rush the first map boss for Hilda's passive, then capture towers and socket precursor tablets before pushing tier.

items.question: Do I need to do both towers and tablets?
answer: Yes, they work together. Towers provide the radius; precursor tablets provide the actual modifiers. A tower with no tablets does little.

items.question: What is the 3-to-1 reforge?
answer: At the reforging bench you can combine three lower-tier waystones into one waystone of the next tier up. It is the safety net when your high-tier pool runs dry.

items.question: Why prioritise Hilda's passive?
answer: It strengthens every map boss you kill, which improves boss loot across your whole Atlas - a permanent power spike for one conversation.
